context:
Goal: a search agent runs Opus only where it judges meaning, is blocked otherwise, and you can allow a one-off.
Problem (money): since your Nov 1 ruling, a search agent on Opus with no audit mark is refused, and only you can say whether the audit mark also unlocks Opus or only Sonnet.
Based on (ruling): your Nov 1 17:25 CST ruling: a model above the role's is refused, and your typed override lifts it.
Based on (read): the model-per-role record gives an audit search Sonnet when its brief carries the mark Audit:, and Opus on your grant of Oct 21.
Departs from: the setup running today lets every search run Opus without asking — Opus for a search only as picked below.

Your question on the earlier idea of letting every search run Opus without asking: it would not need a lift. The guard would never ask, so every search would run Opus silently; a lift only applies where the guard refuses or asks. Your override can be scoped to most roles, but not yet to search agents, so lifting for searches would be a blanket Opus lift. So yes: without a, you cannot keep some searches on Opus and block others.
Your other question, whether every way an agent can get the wrong model is covered: not yet. Four ways still slip through: Opus is only asked about, not refused (your Nov 1 ruling fixes this, being built now); workflow scripts that start many agents skip the model check; an agent with no model named while a default model is set; and a new model name the guard cannot rank, on the Plan and designer roles. Each check was added for one incident, so coverage grew piece by piece; the next two fixes being built close the first two (the Opus refusal and the check on workflow scripts).

options.gain: Deep audits use the best model with no question; plain searches stay cheap.
options.how: A search whose brief carries the audit mark may run Sonnet or Opus; a search on Opus with no mark is refused, and your override lifts it.
options.label: The audit mark unlocks Sonnet or Opus
options.lose: A session can put Opus on any audit without asking you.

options.how: Opus on any search needs your typed override, which gets a search-only form (Opus for searches for 2 hours).
options.label: The audit mark unlocks Sonnet only
options.lose: More stops for you on deep audits.

options.how: Your Oct 21 grant is withdrawn; only your override allows it.
options.label: Never Opus for a search
options.lose: The same stops as b, and the Oct 21 grant is gone.

ref: step explore-audit-marker (the Audit: line on search agents); decision agent-model-cap (model per role)
reply: Pick a taken (saved Nov 1 18:38 CST). The lane explore-audit-marker builds it.
title: Which model may a search agent run: the table says Haiku, Sonnet for an audit, Opus only on your grant; the guard lets any search run Opus
why: Deep audits keep the best model and plain searches stay cheap, with no new stops for you.
